active.title: Kayak the American Narrows
active.description: The channel between Wellesley Island and the mainland delivers sheltered paddling through the densest cluster of private islands in the Thousand Islands chain — no open crossings, just one island-lined corridor after another.
active.bonus: Paddle the full narrows from one end to the other without touching shore. Start to finish.

active.title: Hike Wellesley Island State Park Nature Trails
active.description: Seven miles of trail on the largest public island in the region cross hardwood forest, exposed bedrock, and shoreline bluffs — the nature center section has the best bird and beaver sightings in the whole chain.
active.bonus: Find the osprey nesting platform in the nature center preserve and count every bird you spot before you leave.

active.title: Bike the Seaway Trail: Clayton to Cape Vincent
active.description: Thirty flat miles of Great Lakes Seaway Trail road connect two of the St. Lawrence's quietest towns along an unbroken shoreline with constant water views and almost no shoulder traffic.
active.bonus: Complete the full out-and-back without stopping to check your phone once.

active.title: Paddleboard Heart Island at Dawn
active.description: Get on the water before the tour boats start and slowly circle Heart Island as the river turns pink — Boldt Castle rising from the morning mist is one of the more quietly theatrical views in upstate New York.
active.bonus: Get close enough to the castle stonework to touch it before heading back to shore.

social.title: Sunset at the Clayton Marina Docks
social.description: Clayton's waterfront fills on summer evenings with live-aboards, day-trippers, and locals who know that the St. Lawrence turns gold at 7pm — the dock is the most social square footage in the entire Thousand Islands.
social.bonus: Strike up a conversation with someone on a boat and ask where they're headed next.

social.title: Live Night at Koffee Kove, Clayton
social.description: Clayton's beloved waterfront café turns into a live-music spot after dark — local acts, no cover, and a room full of people who actually live here year-round rather than just in summer.
social.bonus: Request a specific song from the performer between sets — not 'whatever you feel like.' Something particular.

social.title: Friday Night in Alexandria Bay
social.description: Alex Bay goes all-in on summer nights — live music on the waterfront, Boldt Castle lit across the water, and a resort-town energy that hasn't changed much since the 1980s and is better for it.
social.bonus: Stay until the last bar closes. Close your tab at a place you found by walking, not searching.

social.title: Evening at the Antique Boat Museum, Clayton
social.description: The most serious collection of wooden watercraft in North America draws collectors and river people who've been on the St. Lawrence for generations — their event season is the best access you'll ever get.
social.bonus: Find someone who can tell you a firsthand story about a specific boat in the collection before you leave.

chill.title: Watch Freighters Pass at Tibbetts Point Lighthouse
chill.description: Cape Vincent's lighthouse sits at the exact confluence where Lake Ontario empties into the St. Lawrence River — ocean-going freighters pass within 200 yards of the lawn, headed for the Atlantic.
chill.bonus: Stay until at least one vessel passes. Identify its flag and look up what it's carrying before you leave.

chill.title: Afternoon at Sackets Harbor Battlefield
chill.description: The 1812 battlefield on Lake Ontario is one of the most serene historic sites in New York — manicured grounds, unobstructed lake views, and almost no one there on a weekday.
chill.bonus: Read one full interpretive panel at the site without skimming — actually read it.

chill.title: Picnic on Grass Point State Park Beach
chill.description: The small beach at Grass Point gives you a front-row seat to St. Lawrence River traffic — cargo ships, sailboats, and tour boats all pass close enough to read the hull markings.
chill.bonus: Stay for at least two hours without opening a social media app. Not airplane mode — truly not looking.

chill.title: Sunrise from the Thousand Islands Bridge
chill.description: Pull over at the American span's roadside pull-off and watch the sun come up over the river and into Canada — the bridge frame, the water, the 1,800 islands, and the silence. Nothing close to it.
chill.bonus: Get there before the sun fully clears the horizon. If you missed first light, it doesn't count.

foodie.title: Fish Fry Friday at Foxy's, Alexandria Bay
foodie.description: Alex Bay's most beloved waterfront bar has served the definitive Thousand Islands fish fry for decades — beer-battered walleye, cold Labatt's, and a crowd that's been coming here since before you were born.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the bar. Order the walleye. Ask the bartender what they'd eat tonight and order that too.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Koffee Kove, Clayton
foodie.description: Clayton's waterfront institution serves the whole river community from first light — guides fueling up before a dawn muskie trip, boaters nursing coffee at dock tables, and locals with the same order for twenty years.
foodie.bonus: Order the daily special without asking what it is.

foodie.title: Guided Shore Dinner on the River
foodie.description: The old Thousand Islands tradition of cooking freshly caught walleye on a flat riverside rock over an open fire is something you book through a local guide — a meal that exists nowhere else and has fed river people here for generations.
foodie.bonus: Help prep the catch, whatever that involves. You don't get to just watch.

foodie.title: Dinner on the Veranda at Bonnie Castle Resort
foodie.description: Alexandria Bay's Victorian-era resort puts you on an open veranda over the river with Boldt Castle visible from your table — the dining room earns its setting.
foodie.bonus: Order the catch of the day and ask your server where it was pulled from this morning.

adventure.title: Snorkel the Eel Bay Shoals, Wellesley Island
adventure.description: The shoal flats off Wellesley Island offer surprisingly clear freshwater visibility — smallmouth bass, yellow perch, and the occasional muskie in water that's warm by July and clear enough to see thirty feet.
adventure.bonus: Stay in the water long enough to spot a fish longer than your forearm.

adventure.title: Night Tour of Singer Castle, Dark Island
adventure.description: The most theatrical castle in the Thousand Islands sits on a three-acre island near Hammond and runs candlelit evening tours — dungeon, secret passage, towers, and river views that justify the boat ride alone. Book well ahead.
adventure.bonus: Ask your guide to take you through both the dungeon and the secret passage. If they offer a choice, take both.

adventure.title: Full Day Boat Charter from Clayton Marina
adventure.description: Rent a day charter out of Clayton and set your own course through 1,800 islands — visit Boldt Castle, anchor off an uncrowded island for lunch, and make the return run at sunset with the light behind you.
adventure.bonus: Anchor somewhere that isn't on the standard tour route and stay for at least 30 minutes.

adventure.title: Guided Muskie Fishing on the St. Lawrence
adventure.description: The river between Clayton and Gananoque holds some of the best muskie fishing in North America — hire a guide, learn the structure, and fish water the locals don't post about on social media.
adventure.bonus: Land a fish over 36 inches and release it without lifting it out of the water.
